# Sirach Chapter 44 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalent)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 44 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**44:1** Let us now praise famous men — our ancestors, generation after generation.

**44:2** The Lord gave them great glory; his majesty has been theirs from the very beginning.

**44:3** Some of them ruled as kings, famous for their power; some gave counsel through their wisdom and proclaimed prophecies;

**44:4** some led their people in council; some taught the people and showed good sense; some spoke with wisdom in their instruction;

**44:5** some composed musical melodies; some composed poems and set them in writing;

**44:6** some were wealthy men of substance, living quietly in their homes —

**44:7** all of them were honored in their own time, each one glorious in his day.

**44:8** Some left a name that is still remembered, so that people still recount their praise.

**44:9** Others left no memorial; they died as though they had never existed. They might as well never have been born — and so it is with their children after them.

**44:10** But these were men of mercy — their acts of righteousness have not been forgotten.

**44:11** With their descendants, their good deeds live on; their blessings pass down to their children's children.

**44:12** Their descendants hold firm to the covenants; their children stand secure because of them.

**44:13** Their line will endure forever; their glory will never be wiped away.

**44:14** Their bodies rest in peace, but their name lives on from age to age.

**44:15** The peoples will celebrate their wisdom; the whole assembly will announce their praise.

**44:16** Enoch pleased the Lord and was taken up — he stands as a model of repentance for every generation.

**44:17** Noah was found blameless and righteous; when wrath came, he became the means of rescue; because of him a remnant survived when the flood swept over the earth.

**44:18** Everlasting covenants were made with him: that all flesh would never again be swept away in a flood.

**44:19** Abraham was the great father of a host of nations; no one has been found who could match his glory.

**44:20** He kept the law of the Most High and entered into covenant with him; in his own flesh he ratified the covenant; when put to the test he proved faithful.

**44:21** So the Lord promised him with an oath that through his descendants the nations would be blessed; that his descendants would multiply like the dust of the earth, rise up high as the stars, and inherit land from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth.

**44:22** The same promise he confirmed to Isaac, for the sake of Abraham his father — the blessing of all peoples, and the covenant, he let come to rest on Jacob's head.

**44:23** He ratified it with his blessings and gave him his inheritance; he marked out his portions and divided them among twelve tribes.
